subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For Codex-backed turns interrupted after possible side effects, should OpenClaw resume, synthesize a final status, or fail closed with restart-specific recovery guidance when the app-server closes or the Gateway restarts?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses Codex transport failure classification, replay safety, Gateway restart recovery, and channel delivery policy, and upstream Codex does not provide a rich shutdown reason for OpenClaw to consume automatically.

options.title: Design restart-aware recovery
options.body: Create one cross-surface policy for intentional Gateway shutdown, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused Codex/Gateway/channel tests.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics and copy
options.body: Keep runtime behavior fail-closed but make logs and user-facing messages distinguish Gateway restart from unexpected app-server failure.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Keep the issue under live-repro tracking until a current-main long-maintenance run proves the remaining client-close trigger.

recommendation.title: Design restart-aware recovery
recommendation.body: Create one cross-surface policy for intentional Gateway shutdown, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused Codex/Gateway/channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their Codex app-server retry/recovery policy work is the central current behavior that any cross-surface decision must preserve or revise.
